races.name: Broughton Transport The Mane Logistics Choice Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Early Release
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with genuine hold-up tendencies forced into a midfield role by the field composition; David Evans has 3 wins from 23 runners in the last 14 days showing stable in form, and the 50-day break is worth monitoring, but this horse has won twice and placed once on similar going — the out-of-role positioning tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last six starts, including last time out, but that form is patchy elsewhere and this is a first run in 50 days. Raced over today's distance before, breaks from stall 3, and a rating of 68 leaves him sixth of seven.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Best form comes on good ground (3W3P in 10 sim-going runs) and Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim is a useful aid; a natural hold-up horse who should get closer to his true position than some rivals given the 22-day turnaround and the 6-year-old's experience at managing his own race.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back and consistent in this sequence, though below-par when fifth last time. He returns within a month, has raced over today's distance, and rates 80 on our figures - second of seven. Needs to rediscover his best to trouble the front two.

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' runner arrives on a 13-day turnaround in solid recent form (373238) and has placed five times on similar going — a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style gets compressed into midfield here, meaning Chloe Lyons must negotiate gaps on a 5½f course where daylight arrives late; the tv headgear is noted.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts but rarely far away, with three thirds and a second among those runs, though last time's eighth was a step back. Fit again 13 days on, proven over today's trip, and rated 70 - fifth of seven.

runners_data.name: Grey Horizon
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and therefore the pivotal pace-maker; wears a visor, has won and placed on good ground, and Christian Howarth can exploit an uncontested lead — the STYLE_FIT tag is a mild caveat, but as sole pace-setter this horse shapes the entire race.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back, and second last time out, with only one below-par run between. Quick to reappear 12 days on and proven over today's trip, he rates 75 on our figures - fourth of seven - and needs more improvement to reach the front two.

runners_data.name: In The City
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's gelding is a natural prominent racer and the most likely horse to occupy the position directly behind Grey Horizon; Ashley Lewis claims 3lbs, recent form includes a win and place at longer trips, and the step back to 5½f is the key unknown — but good ground form (1W2P from 3 runs) is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts but rarely too far away, finishing no worse than fifth and as close as second. Resumes after 47 days off, but rates 92, clear top pick of seven, with the layoff the only query.

runners_data.name: Saucy Jane
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has won twice on good ground from eight similar-going starts; Mason Paetel rides and the 14-day turnaround looks routine for this yard — a hold-up type who may find the Bath straight too short to produce a telling late run, though a recent second at 6f on good ground shows she can finish.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out, though the form either side is mixed with a couple of modest efforts. Quick to build on that success 14 days on and proven over today's trip, she rates 78 - third of seven - with consistency the only query.

runners_data.name: Reality Queen
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's three-year-old carries the lowest weight at 121lbs which is a notable advantage; a hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position by the field composition — Liam Wright will need a very tidy passage, and sim-going record (1W1P from 4) is modest, so the style displacement is a real concern at this short trip.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out, but that snapped a sequence of modest efforts, including two sevenths. Quick to confirm the form 14 days on and with today's distance proven, she's only 61 on our figures - bottom of the field - so needs to repeat rather than revert.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Horizon is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only In The City as a genuine second prominent type, faces minimal early pressure across this 5½f at Bath — a setup that allows Grey Horizon to bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo rather than being forced into a draining speed duel. In The City will likely sit just off the pace in second, but with no other horse capable of matching Grey Horizon's early position, the leader dictates terms from the outset and can conserve energy through the middle section before the final climb. This field contains significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate: Early Release, Merrimack, and Reality Queen are all genuine hold-up types but have been mapped to midfield because there simply is not room for them all at the rear — of those three, Merrimack's recent sharpness and Early Release's winning form at the trip make them the most likely to push furthest forward from that group, but none should be expected to race in their true natural position. The race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles — a controlled lead for Grey Horizon means the hold-up horses face a long, potentially futile chase on a track that does not consistently reward late finishers, particularly over this shorter trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grey Horizon Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Horizon gets a clean break and controls tempo without being pressed by In The City or any redistributed midfield horse.
scenarios.body: Grey Horizon sets a comfortable gallop, the hold-up horses are stuck in traffic or too far back to close on a short 5½f track, and the leader has enough in reserve to hold on up the Bath straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If In The City tracks Grey Horizon closely and challenges entering the final two furlongs, turning it into a two-horse battle.
scenarios.body: The pace is genuine but not suicidal, and any horse with a prominent early position is ideally placed while hold-up runners scramble from deep; the winner emerges from the front two.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Picks Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Horizon sets a stronger-than-expected pace and ties up in the closing stages, opening the door for a fast-finishing hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: Merrimack or Safari Dream, racing from a genuine hold-up position, find a clear run and pick off a tiring leader, but the short trip and track profile makes this a secondary scenario given the redistribution of natural closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble Late Drama
scenarios.trigger: If early pace collapses or traffic problems disrupt the prominent horses, creating a bunched finish with no clear pace advantage.
scenarios.body: Saucy Jane or Reality Queen, racing with freshness and lower weights, capitalise on a chaotic finish, though their true hold-up styles make this a low-probability outcome heavily dependent on pace collapse.

watchPoints.text: Grey Horizon — if this horse jumps cleanly and immediately goes to the front unchallenged, the entire race dynamic falls into its favour and the hold-up horses have almost no time to close on 5½f at Bath.

Early Release and Merrimack — both are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield; watch whether they actually push forward at the start or drop in naturally, as their true position will materially affect which scenario plays out.

In The City — the step down from 7-8f to 5½f is a significant trip reduction; if this horse gets outpaced early and cannot track Grey Horizon, Scenario B collapses entirely and Scenario A becomes even more dominant.

Safari Dream — of all the genuine hold-up types, this six-year-old has the strongest similar-going record (3W3P) and Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim; if any late finisher is to threaten, this is the one to track through the field in the final furlong.

Reality Queen's weight — at 121lbs versus rivals at 133-138lbs, the 12-17lb weight advantage is significant in a flat handicap and worth monitoring at the off price, even if the style displacement and modest going record limit confidence in the run shape.

races.name: Resolution Canter Cup EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bellatina
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record — four times in the first three over 5f on good — but her natural hold-up style is mapped to midfield given the surplus of closers in this field, which means she may not get the cover she needs; placed form on similar ground is her strongest asset.|

runners_data.name: Dissenter
runners_data.note: Unbeaten potential debutant angle for Tregoning at OR=120, with a sole run of fifth over 6f on Firm; her tactical identity is unknown and she may naturally stride forward, which in this pace-vacuum race is a positional gift.|

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Four runs without a placing and a record that suggests she tends to find little in the closing stages; her true hold-up style is pushed into midfield by the field's composition, compounding a weak finishing profile on this evidence.|

runners_data.name: Sayidah Ardad
runners_data.note: Placed second on good ground over 6f gives her the best placed form among the confirmed hold-up runners; Grace Harris sends her out with modest T14 numbers and a 30-day break, so freshness is neutral rather than a flag.|

runners_data.name: Sheer Beauty
runners_data.note: One run into sixth over 5f on good for the Birkett yard, which is lightly active (T14:1/5); her tactical role is entirely unknown and she could default to a prominent position off a flat break, making her interesting in an uncontested-pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Space Dreamer
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly finished fifth over this exact trip and going combination, giving her the most comparable recent prep in the field; Charles Bishop (T14:3/17) rides for a trainer with modest but active numbers and she is fresh enough at 44 days to bounce.|

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny
runners_data.note: Three runs without threatening the frame, including two sixths and a fifth — the form is thin and her genuine hold-up style is squeezed into midfield by the race structure, so she is essentially racing blind tactically and her finishing kick has not shown itself to date.|

runners_data.name: Yankeedoodledandy
runners_data.note: Two runs, both finishing eighth or worse on good ground over 6f, with a fading-in-finish flag attached; Taylor Fisher takes over but the raw form gives no grounds for optimism in any scenario, regardless of pace shape.|

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field and the majority of runners — Bellatina, Last Dandelion, Tricky Jenny, Sayidah Ardad, and Yankeedoodledandy — all carrying hold-up profiles, this 5f contest at Bath is set up as a slow-burn drift into a compressed sprint finish, with no horse likely to stride clear early and build a meaningful lead. The three unraced or lightly-raced runners — Dissenter, Space Dreamer, and Sheer Beauty — carry unknown tactical identities and one or more of them may default to a prominent position simply by jumping and travelling forward without restraint, effectively creating pace by accident rather than design. This field holds more natural hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Bellatina, Last Dandelion, and Tricky Jenny are all tagged as redistributed, meaning at least some of them will be racing out of their natural role and unable to get the cover they need. The tactical verdict is clear — horses with a prominent or front-running profile, or lightly-raced runners capable of racing handily without burning up, hold a structural edge here, as a field without a genuine pace-setter rewards those who travel into the race naturally rather than those forced into an unfamiliar position chasing a ragged tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Unknown Types Lead Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of Dissenter, Space Dreamer, or Sheer Beauty travels forward naturally from the break and sets an uncontested early tempo without burning out.
scenarios.body: With no established front-runner, a lightly-raced filly who settles in a prominent position can dictate on her own terms over the sharp Bath 5f, never facing a sustained pace challenge from behind. Dissenter (OR=120) and Space Dreamer (OR=120) both carry class unexposed form and their handlers may allow them to stride forward freely, giving them a positional advantage that the hold-up brigade cannot overcome.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Squeeze Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely crawling to halfway and the field bunches, allowing the strongest finisher to sprint through from midfield in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop compresses the field and turns the final 2f into a flat-out dash, which theoretically suits a horse with a high cruising speed and good finishing kick. Bellatina — who has shown consistent placed form and races on a sound surface — and Sayidah Ardad, with a second at 6f on good, are best positioned among the hold-up types to land this shape, though their redistributed mapping tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Prominent Sails Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one runner breaks smartly and crosses unchallenged into a clear lead while the hold-up pack traffic-jams behind.
scenarios.body: Over Bath's undulating 5f, a horse allowed to bowl along at a comfortable solo gallop can steal enough margin in the first half to repel late challenges, especially if the closers are forced wide or get no run. Sheer Beauty or Space Dreamer, both with only one run under their belt and potentially underestimated on pace, could exploit precisely this vacuum.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Lands Debut
scenarios.trigger: If a heavily-backed newcomer or lightly-raced runner defies a modest field on class alone regardless of pace shape.
scenarios.body: OR=120 runners Dissenter, Sheer Beauty, and Space Dreamer all have the ceiling to win a Band D maiden purely on ability, and if any fires on debut form the tactical picture becomes secondary. Dissenter, trained by Marcus Tregoning with a fifth on Firm over 6f behind her, is the most likely candidate to land this shape if she simply outclasses the opposition in the stretch.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dissenter, Space Dreamer, or Sheer Beauty — all lightly-raced OR=120 runners — jump and travel prominently from the stalls, as the first to occupy the lead in this pace-less field immediately gains a structural advantage no hold-up runner can easily neutralise.

Bellatina's displaced mapping is a live risk to her backers — she is a natural hold-up filly in a field so stuffed with closers that she cannot get her preferred position, and a slow early tempo with traffic may strangle her chance entirely.

Tricky Jenny and Last Dandelion share a near-identical profile: genuine hold-up style, no placed form, and both redistributed to midfield — if the race drifts into a sprint finish and they get no daylight, they are likely to be squeezed out of the picture.

Yankeedoodledandy carries a fades-in-finish flag on both career runs over 6f — dropping to 5f at Bath might appear to help, but the consistent non-finishing pattern at this yard (J S Moore T14:1/15) suggests her chance is structural rather than distance-related.

Going is listed as unknown across all Bath going reports — if the strip is faster than expected, the lightly-raced OR=120 runners who have already shown competence on good turf (Space Dreamer, Sheer Beauty) hold a relative edge over hold-up fillies relying on a slow early tempo to compress the field.

races.name: Home Group Financial Wealth Management Trophy Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Recorded a course win at this exact five furlongs on good ground and the sim-going record (9/15) is the strongest in the field; a natural hold-up runner but has placed twice at this trip, and at age 8 is well-exposed, though John Gallagher's yard has been quiet over 14 days (0/6) which tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after two moderate efforts, with a third earlier in this sequence and a pair of unplaced runs further back — the pre-win blip is the query. Rated second on our figures and race-fit 18 days on, he remains a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Darkened Edge
runners_data.note: The key pace influence here — Christopher Mason's yard is in solid form (3/7 over 14 days) and this horse has won at this course and distance on good ground; tagged with a style-fit flag for racing out of its ideal prominent role, but in this context it IS the front-runner by default, making that flag less damaging than usual.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after a modest run whose best previously was third. Quick to race again 12 days on, with form over today's trip, but ranked only fourth on our figures, needing more to confirm that was no flash.

runners_data.name: Little Miss Magic
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings has been quiet (0/8 over 14 days) and this mare's five-run history shows a preference for six furlongs rather than five; a genuine hold-up horse at heart, shunted into a midfield map position because the field is stacked with late-runners, and the visor (headgear) adds a small unknown; sim-going record of just 5/15 on similar ground is modest.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to end a run of modest finishes, and tops this field on our figures at 62. The only slight concern is the 27-day gap since that win, though she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: The only three-year-old in the field, racing off OR 57, and yet to win or place in 15 similar-going runs; Scott Dixon's yard is moderate at 1/12 over 14 days, and this horse's natural hold-up style is compressed into midfield given the field composition — five furlongs may also be sharper than ideal based on its form profile over six.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last six starts but rarely out of the frame, following an eighth with four finishes in the 4-6 range including one last time out. Fit again 19 days on, has form over today's trip and sits third of these on our figures.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Hope
runners_data.note: Grace Harris has been busy (2/15 over 14 days) but without great success; an 8-year-old carrying the lowest weight alongside Coast, and a true hold-up horse whose three similar-going wins/places came over six furlongs — mapped into midfield by necessity, not by choice, and the five-furlong trip on a track favouring pace looks a difficult ask.
runners_data.comment: Rated only 50 by our figures, some way behind the principals, though he did finish fourth last time out after a below-par eighth. Without a win in his last six starts and needs to find more again over today's trip to feature at this level.

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Ran just eight days ago and returns quickly for Scott Dixon; another genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield map role because of the field's composition, though its recent form string includes a couple of placed efforts at six furlongs on good — the step down to five at Bath, combined with its natural waiting style, makes this a structurally awkward race for it to win.
runners_data.comment: Bottom-rated of these on our figures but ran with credit into third last time out, backing up a fifth before that. Quick to race again 8 days on, and though without a win in her last six starts, that form keeps her of interest over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Darkened Edge is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and, crucially, faces no direct rival likely to push the pace hard from the gates — the remaining five runners are all hold-up or prominent types by nature. That creates a controlled, single-speed gallop from Darkened Edge over Bath's five furlongs, where an uncontested leader can dictate rhythm and deny closers the strong pace they need to close ground in the final furlong. Little Miss Magic, Symbol Of Hope, and Coast are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions on the map because the field is saturated with runners who prefer racing from the rear; in reality, none of them are likely to gain the front-running position that would suit them most, and their finishing kicks depend on a pace that simply may not materialise. This race shape firmly favours a horse that can travel prominently, control the tempo, and sustain its effort — the profile that benefits most is a prominent racer or converted front-runner that doesn't need to be produced late against a modest pace injection.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Darkened Edge Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Darkened Edge breaks cleanly and settles into an uncontested front-running role with no rival applying early pressure.
scenarios.body: Darkened Edge dictates a moderate, controlled gallop and quickens clear in the final furlong before the true hold-up horses can make meaningful inroads; at Bath's sharp five furlongs, a horse controlling tempo from the front is notoriously difficult to reel in when the pace is honest but not suicidal. Runners who can travel in its slipstream and launch from a close-up position are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Handsheikh or Beach Partee push forward early and create a genuine two-horse duel for the lead, lifting the pace.
scenarios.body: A contested pace increases the likelihood that neither leader finishes strongly, opening a narrow window for a closer to rattle home late down the centre of the track. However, with most hold-up runners genuinely displaced from their preferred deep position, any finishing surge will be limited in scale.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and the genuine hold-up horses — despite poor positioning — find enough room to weave through.
scenarios.body: Symbol Of Hope or Coast would need to be switched off further back than their map position suggests and produce a strong late run, but this scenario is structurally undermined because all three redistributed closers are unlikely to be truly held up and therefore won't generate the sectional differential needed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Darkened Edge is pushed wide or stumbles early, chaos disrupts the expected shape and the race devolves into a moderate-tempo scramble.
scenarios.body: With no replacement pace-setter and several horses out of their natural role, the race loses its shape and becomes a messy affair where positional advantage from the gate decides the result. Low-draw, handy types benefit most from the resulting bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Darkened Edge's early strides — if it fails to break cleanly or is pushed wide by a rival, the entire pace structure of the race dissolves and the favourite scenario collapses immediately.

Monitor whether Secret Handsheikh attempts to press forward from the gate; if the gelding does, it creates a contested pace that dramatically shortens the expected lead advantage for Darkened Edge and opens the race up.
Little Miss Magic's visor is noted headgear that can sharpen a horse's early behaviour — watch for it racing more keenly than expected, which could inject pace where none was anticipated.

Coast's quick turnaround (8 days since last run) for a hold-up horse over a shorter trip than it has placed at is worth monitoring in running — if it gets a poor early position it will likely have nothing to work with in a low-pace scenario.

Beach Partee is the sole three-year-old taking on older, more experienced sprinters; watch for how Christian Howarth (claim) manages its position early, as a poor start from this age group at Bath's tight five furlongs often proves impossible to recover from.

races.name: Novacast Don't Come Last Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Man Of The Sea
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old hold-up specialist under Taylor Fisher whose entire profile is built around staying trips on good ground — 13 of 15 similar-going runs have produced a finish, though his last win came some time ago and he has been placed just once in five recent starts, flagging diminishing returns at OR 54.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back but modest since, including a below-par ninth two runs ago, with a better fourth last time out. Fit again 14 days on and proven over today's trip, he rates 56 - third of five - with that indifferent middle patch the main risk.

runners_data.name: Assured
runners_data.note: Finley Marsh takes the mount on a five-year-old who arrives on a 54-day break for Tom Gretton, whose stable has shown no recent winners; naturally races from the rear but the redistribution to midfield reflects the reality that there is no pace to chase in this field, which blunts his hold-up game.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts and never better than fifth in that run, with this a first outing in 54 days. She has raced over today's trip before, rates 53 - fourth of five - and the long absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: Syd Hosie's four-year-old has consistent placed form at 16-17f on good ground and is arguably the most proven horse at today's trip and conditions, though Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim is the main positive — the horse's genuine back-to-back placing record at this distance counts in his favour even with a style forced slightly forward.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts but rarely too far away, including a second two runs back. She's had a 33-day break, has raced over today's trip before, and rates 57 - second of five - with fitness after the gap the only query.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old arrives on a 14-day turnaround with Luke Morris booked, and the yard's 2/12 strike rate in the last 14 days is worth noting; her form is limited to shorter trips and an all-weather surface, but she holds the highest OR in the field at 61 and Morris's tactical acumen in a race without natural pace could prove decisive.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last four starts but improving fast, stepping up markedly when second last time out after three modest efforts. Back within a fortnight, she tops our figures at 59 - just shy of her official mark - with confirming that improvement the only query.

runners_data.name: Endofastorm
runners_data.note: Joe Ponting's seven-year-old has posted six consecutive placed or winning efforts at 10-12f, giving him a strong profile of consistency, but today's 14f trip is a genuine step up in distance and as a hold-up type finding himself redistributed to midfield he must prove he can travel positively enough to deliver his effort without the strong pace he typically needs.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last six starts despite three seconds, and this is a first run in 32 days. She has raced over today's trip before, but rates only 49 - bottom of the five - so plentiful places alone won't be enough here.

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners carrying a hold-up profile, there is no natural front-runner in this field, and the race is likely to crawl in its early stages before developing into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs at Bath. Man Of The Sea and Campeona are the most likely to press forward by default given the absence of genuine pace, though neither is a natural leader; Campeona's recent second over 12f on Fibresand suggests she can quicken when the tempo is modest. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place cleanly — Assured, Blue Siam, and Endofastorm are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, and all three face the reality that there is simply no pace to chase. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours the horse with the most tactical versatility and the ability to find a position just off a non-existent pace, then produce a controlled late effort — a profile that suits a horse ridden with positional intelligence rather than a deep closer who needs a true-run gallop to build momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Campeona Dictates Slowly
scenarios.trigger: If Campeona is sent forward to fill the pace vacuum and controls a crawl before quickening off the turn.
scenarios.body: Luke Morris can exploit the absence of front-runners by sending Campeona to the front and controlling a falsely-run race at a conservative tempo, allowing her natural class edge at OR 61 — the highest in the field — to assert when she kicks on entering the straight. Her recent second over 12f represents a significant drop back in experience at this trip but her yard is in good form and Morris is an astute tactician who rarely gets caught cold in false-run races.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If no horse takes charge and the field crawls before bunching, turning the final two furlongs into a sprint.
scenarios.body: A truly falsely-run race compresses the field and randomises the finish, making the final position from the home turn critical; whoever lands widest or gets the cleanest passage into the straight has the advantage. Man Of The Sea has the second-highest OR and consistent good-ground form over staying trips, while Endofastorm's recent back-to-back placed efforts at 12f on good ground give him a live chance in a bunch finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Blue Siam Creeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Siam gets a trouble-free run through the compressed field and times a late run to perfection under a positive Tucker ride.
scenarios.body: Blue Siam has three consecutive placed efforts at 16-17f on good ground and clearly handles this trip well, making him a natural beneficiary if the race sets up for a steady-run closer who can stalk the pace from midfield. Charlie Tucker claims 7lb which is meaningful at this level, though Blue Siam's true hold-up style means he requires the race to develop in a way that creates space — not guaranteed in a five-runner crawl.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Assured Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picked up earlier than expected and Assured gets a clear run to unleash his best closing effort.
scenarios.body: Assured has been well beaten in recent starts and arrives on a 54-day break, but Finley Marsh can hunt cover and deliver a late challenge if the tempo finally quickens mid-race rather than turning into a pure sprint. His poor recent form and layoff make this the least reliable outcome, and as a redistributed hold-up type forced into midfield he may struggle to find his rhythm in a race that lacks the true gallop he needs.

watchPoints.text: Watch Campeona's early positioning — if Luke Morris sends her forward from the outset to fill the pace vacuum, she commands this race on OR and tactical terms.
Blue Siam's Charlie Tucker claim is the most significant weight concession in the field at 7lb — watch whether he can settle Blue Siam in a workable position given a crawling early tempo.
Endofastorm's trip stamina is unproven beyond 12f today; if the race develops late pace and his hold-up run is delayed by traffic in a bunched five-runner field, his chance evaporates.

Man Of The Sea has run 13 times on similar going without a win and only one placing in his last five — watch whether the pace dynamic actually creates the late sprint his profile demands before taking him at short prices.
Assured's 54-day break for a yard without a recent winner is a combination that typically requires a run to find peak condition — watch market moves for any sign of stable confidence.

races.name: Wiltshire And Bath Air Ambulance Charity Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yokkell
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up horse with 1W2P on similar going and placed over 10f on good ground last time; 22 days since last run is straightforward, but natural style means he needs a stronger gallop than Man Is King is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts but competitive throughout, with a third three runs back, and a fair fourth last time out. Back within a month, she tops our figures at 70, clear of this field, with turning that into a win the only question.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: Multiple placed efforts over 12f on good and standard going give this 8-year-old hold-up type reasonable credentials, though the headgear (p) and a trainer in modest form (0/2 over 14 days) temper expectations; needs pace to be injected to close meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last six starts and without a placed effort in her last four, though a third six starts back shows more ability. Quick to reappear 14 days on and proven over today's trip, she rates 64 - third of eight - with recent form the query.

runners_data.name: Bug Boy
runners_data.note: Decent placed record over 12f on soft ground but only 1W3P on similar, and this 10-year-old's true hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield slot — the race shape is unlikely to produce the gallop he needs to deliver his best effort at this stage of his career.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last four starts but rarely too far away, with a fourth the best of that sequence. This is a first run in 39 days, though proven over today's trip, and he rates 65 - second of eight - with the layoff the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Man Is King
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter, and with a win at 10f on good ground and a tongue-tie fitted, Gordon can dictate a comfortable tempo; his STYLE_FIT flag notes he is racing slightly out of role, but in a field of closers he is structurally advantaged regardless.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last six starts but both a while back now, with a modest sixth his most recent effort. Quick to reappear 15 days on and proven over today's trip, he rates 59 - fifth of eight - and needs to rediscover that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Hope Rising
runners_data.note: Strong form over much longer distances (2/16f, 2/18f, 3/20f all on good) makes her a genuine stayer stepping back in trip, and her prominent style means she should travel close to Man Is King without stress; Jamie Snowden's stable is in modest form (1/8) but the horse's consistency in frame finishes is the compelling angle.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts and below-par when unplaced last time out, though sixths and sevenths before that showed more resistance. Quick to bounce back 17 days on and proven over today's trip, she rates 61 - fourth of eight - with repeating that better form the question.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Mark
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old whose two most recent form efforts show a 2nd over 10f on firm and a 5th over 12f on good; his natural hold-up style is mapped mid-field here because the rear is overcrowded, and with a STYLE_FIT flag his chance is structurally dependent on conditions he is unlikely to receive.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts but not without ability. Second two runs back was a promising level, though fifth last time out was a step back. This is a first run in 30 days, though proven over today's trip, and he rates 58 - sixth of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Offiah's Boy
runners_data.note: Recent form of 87-005 is modest and his runs at 12f on firm and soft sit slightly off today's going profile; his true closer style cannot be accommodated at the back of this field, meaning his best chance is being caught wide in the straight rather than executing a textbook hold-up finish.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts and unplaced in two of them, with only a fifth last time out to show for recent efforts. Fit again 14 days on and proven over today's trip, but he rates 53 - bottom of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Cezarro
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old with 0W1P on similar going and a 9-day turnaround, stepping up in trip to 1m3½f; his closes-from-the-rear profile is displaced to midfield here, and with the lowest OR in the field (47) he faces a significant class ceiling even if the race falls his way.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts and well below form when eighth last time out, though a third two runs back hints at more ability. Quick to reappear just nine days on and proven over today's trip, he rates 56, seventh of eight on our figures. That latest effort remains the concern.

races.paceDynamic: Man Is King is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him from the front, Josephine Gordon can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m3½f trip at Bath. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Bug Boy, Jimmy Mark, Offiah's Boy, and Cezarro are all natural closers redistributed into midfield slots on the pace map simply because the rear of the field is overcrowded; they will not naturally take up prominent positions. Hope Rising carries a prominent style tag and represents the most credible secondary challenger for early positioning, but her form profile is built around staying trips considerably longer than today's distance. With Man Is King able to roll along uncontested and set a measured tempo, this race shape heavily favours prominent racers who can track the leader without expending energy and pick up when the pace is controlled — deep hold-up horses dependent on a true gallop are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Man Is King Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King leads unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried pace that suits prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: Man Is King rolls along in front with Hope Rising tracking in second, and the absence of any genuine pace pressure means the race is run to suit those who travel close to the fretting point; closers off a slow gallop are left with insufficient momentum to close the gap. Horses who can sit within two lengths of the leader and produce a clean turn for home benefit most from this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King sets a modest pace but weakens in the final two furlongs, allowing a prominent tracker to overhaul him.
scenarios.body: Hope Rising, who has solid form over longer trips on good ground and regularly finishes in the frame, can sit handily and use her stamina to grind past a fading leader; her consistent placed form at 2/16f, 2/18f, and 3/20f shows she stays well and handles this going. Yokkell, who has placed on similar ground, could also make a late run from just off the pace if the tempo drops enough to make the closing stages genuinely competitive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the field strings out, giving genuine hold-up horses a closing run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the redistributed hold-up types — Bug Boy, Jimmy Mark, or Offiah's Boy — to actually get back into their natural position and find a genuinely strong gallop to close into, both of which are structurally unlikely given Man Is King's lone-leader status and their displaced map positions. Sea Of Charm, a natural hold-up type on good ground with multiple placed efforts over 12f, is best positioned of the closers if the race does develop an unexpectedly strong pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Race Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King is checked, stumbles, or the field bunches unpredictably causing a chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: In a scrambled finish the race becomes a lottery, but horses at the lower end of the weights like Cezarro — a young, lightly-raced 4-year-old who has placed over 10-11f on good ground — could benefit from the disruption; his 4th and 3rd places on comparable going show residual ability that might surface in a muddled race. This scenario is the lowest probability precisely because the field has one clear pace-maker and no evidence of interference factors.

watchPoints.text: Man Is King — if Josephine Gordon allows the gallop to drop to a crawl in the middle mile, the race becomes a sprint for home and his front-running rivals will have nothing to run at, dramatically increasing his chance of lasting to the line.

Hope Rising — watch her jumping position out of the stalls; if she misses the break and cannot get to her natural prominent spot behind Man Is King, her chance is significantly diminished given how dependent this scenario is on tracking the leader.

Bug Boy, Jimmy Mark, Offiah's Boy — monitor in-running; if any of these displaced hold-up types attempt to push forward early to claim a more natural position, it could inject unexpected pace and transform the race shape from a controlled lead scenario to something more genuinely contested.

Sea Of Charm — headgear (p) noted; if the blinkers sharpen her early, she could take closer order than her hold-up tag suggests, though her trainer's 0/2 record over 14 days is a mild dampener on her claims.

Cezarro — freshest horse in the field at 9 days since last run and the lightest weight at 129lbs; at his age and OR level he is worth watching for improvement as the trip tests him, but his structural disadvantage in this pace shape is significant.

races.name: Stakes Are Always High Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Havana Club
runners_data.note: Four recent runs at 8f on Good or Firm show no wins and no places on Good going (sim-going 3/15); a genuine hold-up type placed in midfield on this map, so its chance depends on more pace than this race is likely to generate — trainer Adrian Wintle is 2/10 over 14 days which offers little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last six starts, though he was runner-up three back. Fourth last time out with a sixth in between, he is fit again 16 days on, proven over today's trip and rated third in this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Blue Hero
runners_data.note: Sole career win came over 8f on Firm, and he steps back from longer trips here; a true closer by style who is mapped to midfield rather than the rear only because the field is stacked with hold-up horses — still needs a stronger gallop than Weston Court is likely to supply.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after a moderate run of finishes, quick to back it up just 14 days on and with solid form over today's trip. Only sixth of these on our figures, though, so more needed to confirm that was no fluke.

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with three places at 8f on Good going from 8 similar-surface runs, showing consistency without wins; his natural hold-up style means he sits in midfield on the map by necessity, and with trainer T14 at 0/6 there is no in-form handler boost to draw on.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts, fading to 8th then 6th having been runner-up earlier in that sequence. A 30-day break since that latest run is a query, but he owns a strong speed figure and has form over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Highest-rated horse in the race at OR 60, wearing a hood and with a win at 8f on Standard-equivalent going; his hold-up style is his natural mode but he has the class edge here, and with three placed efforts at 8f from three starts at the trip on Tapeta/AW the concern is whether Bath's turf setting on unknown going replicates those conditions.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and has form over today's trip, freshened by a 20-day layoff following a below-par seventh last time. Rated top of this field on our figures at 58, but must defy 140 lb from stall 4 after two so-so efforts since that win.

runners_data.name: My Ambition
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has placed at 8f on Good, Firm and Standard going (6/15 sim-going) but without a win in this record; ends up in midfield on the map because the rear is crowded with hold-up types, and a trainer strike rate of 0/7 over 14 days provides no current form signal to upgrade his chance.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts but was runner-up and third in two of them, rounding out with a solid fourth last time after an offday ninth. Race-fit 11 days on, has form over today's trip and rated second on our figures.

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up to a mile for the first time after four runs at 6-7f; wears a tongue-tie and is trained by Andrew Balding who is a strong 11/58 over 14 days — the yard form is the most compelling angle here, though the first attempt at the mile trip on unknown Bath going is a genuine unknown.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last four starts but has never finished worse than sixth, banking a workmanlike level of finishes and fit again 18 days on. Proven over today's trip, and with the form bunched near the top, she's fancied to feature strongly on that consistency.

runners_data.name: Weston Court
runners_data.note: Mapped to the lead by redistribution — naturally a hold-up type pushed forward by default as the most likely early pace-setter in an otherwise hold-up-dominated field; carries headgear (visor), is 7 days fresh, and his sim-going record of 7/15 with 0W1P at 8f on Good is uninspiring, so stealing a march is his only realistic route to involvement.
runners_data.comment: Rated only 39 by our figures, some way below these rivals, but the form is trending the right way with a runner-up effort last time out. Quick to run again 7 days on, though he needs more over today's trip to trouble this field.

runners_data.name: Whisper Of Mist
runners_data.note: Returning after 63 days off for a trainer with no runners in the 14-day window; flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a significant negative in a slowly-run race that will be decided by a late kick — hold-up type placed in midfield purely because the back of the field is already occupied, with form reading 0-0-6 in three runs.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures on 32 and without a win in her last three starts, though the form did improve to sixth last time out. A 63-day absence since is a big query, and she needs plenty more to figure over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Weston Court is the sole horse mapped to the lead, though this is a redistribution — a naturally hold-up type pressed into the role of pace-setter by default in a field where no confirmed front runner exists. With no genuine front-runner in the race, the early gallop is likely to be modest and self-regulating, with Weston Court setting a sustainable pace that does little to stretch the field. The bulk of the field — Havana Club, Blue Hero, Rival, My Ambition, and Whisper Of Mist — are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the true race shape will see a compressed, slowly-run contest with most runners travelling in a tight bunch. This race shape strongly favours the horse who can travel closest to the pace with the least trouble in running and produce a decisive finish from a prominent position — given the false pace scenario, a horse that can sit just off the lead and kick early holds a significant positional advantage over those needing a truly strong gallop to deliver from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Weston Court Leads, Modest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Weston Court sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the field idles behind in a bunch, the race becomes a positional contest decided in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mbappe, wearing a hood and with course form over 8f on similar going, is ideally suited to lobbing just off the pace and producing a sustained run; Thai Princess steps up to a mile for the first time but has shown a tendency to travel prominently and could be closer than her form suggests.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is so slow that the field concertinas entering the straight, creating a chaotic sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With no true front-runner present, the race could turn into a sprint from two furlongs out, suiting any horse with natural speed to travel mid-race; Mbappe's 1W2P record on similar going and Rival's placed record at the trip make them the logical beneficiaries of a scramble.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and a genuine hold-up type gets a clear passage off the final bend.
scenarios.body: Blue Hero's sole win came over 8f on Firm, he steps back to a mile in a race that could play to patient closers if the field strings out; Havana Club has placed form at 8f on Good and could benefit if gaps emerge late, though both are racing somewhat out of natural role here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If positional chaos in the bunch sees fancied runners blocked and a lightly-weighted outsider slips clear.
scenarios.body: Whisper Of Mist and Weston Court carry the lowest OR ratings and minimum weight; Whisper Of Mist is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish so is unlikely to win this shape, but Weston Court — if it pinches a lead it naturally holds — could steal a march on a field of hold-up types slow to react.

watchPoints.text: Weston Court's redistribution to the lead is artificial — if it drops away quickly from the front after the first couple of furlongs, the entire field could idle and create a false-pace scenario that benefits whoever is travelling best at the two-furlong pole.

Mbappe's hood (headgear) may sharpen his early focus, but if he is held up deeper than usual behind a pedestrian Weston Court, he risks getting boxed in by the congested hold-up cluster in mid-division — watch how Dylan Hogan positions him from the gate.

Thai Princess's yard form (Balding 11/58 T14) is the standout trainer angle in the race, but she is unproven at a mile and her four runs have all come at 6-7f — a soft or muddling pace could find her outstayed late if the mile trip exposes a stamina limit.

Blue Hero drops back from 10-12f to 8f today after a run at 12f on Good — the trip contraction could sharpen him, but his true style needs a genuine pace to close into and this race is unlikely to supply it.

Whisper Of Mist's 63-day absence and a fading-in-finish flag together make her a horse to monitor early — if she shows any early signs of rustiness or detachment from the pack in a race run at a crawl, she is effectively a non-runner for practical purposes.
